subject: Request for exception: service-credit cap and SLO language - Cobalt Tech
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cobalttech.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@cobalttech.com>, legal@cobalttech.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: cap on service credits / SLO tweak

David —

Thanks for the run-through last week. We’re eager to move forward but Legal/Procurement pushed back on the unlimited-service-credit exposure in the standard Redwood SLO language. For enterprise security and budgeting we need two non-standard items in the contract:

- A cap on cumulative service credits equal to one month of fees in any 12 month period.
- A narrow SLO for the streaming inference endpoint: 99.9% regional uptime rather than the 99.95% proposed for multi-region.

These are gating items for our CFO. The rest of the commercial terms (pricing, term) look good. I attached a short request doc with our preferred language (Cobalt_SLA_Request_v2.pdf). Please let me know if you need anything else for exec review.

—Lena
Lena Ortiz
VP Engineering, Cobalt Tech
Attachment: Cobalt_SLA_Request_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cobalttech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: cap on service credits / SLO tweak

Lena —

Appreciate the clarity and the doc. I can confirm we’re willing to discuss a hard cap on cumulative credits for this renewal given the strategic nature of the account, but that requires an exception to our standard remedy policy and executive signoff.

I’ve looped in Marissa (AE) to provide deal economics and will escalate to ops and finance. Expect an update by EOD Thursday with a recommended binding amendment.

Quick Q: is Cobalt comfortable with the cap applying to credits only (no additional termination rights or financial penalties)? That would make approval more straightforward.

Thanks —
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: cap on service credits / SLO tweak — deal context

Grace —

Forwarding Cobalt’s request. Deal snapshot: 12-month committed term, ARR ~$750k, expected kickoff Jan. Revenue and reference value are high. Procurement insists on the credit cap; legal sent a redline that would limit remedies to credits capped at 100% of one-month fees. Deal desk reviewed and flagged departure from our standard unlimited credits clause.

My recommended path: approve a one-month credit cap tied to invoice month (not cumulative % of contract) and keep the SLO at 99.9% regional for the streaming API. We can add a clause for accelerated remediation (root-cause RCA within 7 business days) to mitigate risk.

If leadership signs off, I’ll prepare the amendment and get Legal to inline the exact language.

-M
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Attachment: Cobalt_Contract_Redline_20261112.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: cap on service credits / SLO tweak — ops review

Marissa / David —

Reviewed the redline and the risk profile. Key points:
- Standard Redwood remedy is service credits calculated pro rata with no explicit upper cap; that is our default for platform reliability.
- Cobalt’s ask (one-month invoice cap) materially limits their downside and our exposure — operationally acceptable if we secure the following:
  1) SLO scoped to a single region (explicitly defined endpoints/IPs)
  2) RCA and mitigation obligations (we commit to post-incident RCA within 7 business days)
  3) Quarterly performance review and the option to re-open terms at renewal if breach frequency exceeds thresholds

Given the strategic value and the ARR, I support granting the cap as a limited exception with the above guardrails. This needs exec approval for a deviation from remedy policy. I’ve put a draft amendment outline in the HubSpot link below for deal desk review.

Grace O'Connor
Head, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8421
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec signoff request — Cobalt Tech service-credit cap (DEAL-8421)

Aditya —

Requesting executive approval to accept a one-month invoice cap on cumulative service credits for Cobalt Tech in exchange for keeping the deal economics intact. Summary:
- ARR: ~$750k; strategic reference customer in fintech vertical.
- Customer asks: cap cumulative credits to one invoice month in any 12-month period; SLO scoped to single-region 99.9% uptime for streaming endpoint.
- Proposed Redwood terms (recommended): Accept cap for credits only (no termination or additional monetary remedies). Add requirement for RCA within 7 business days and quarterly review clause.
- Risk: Limits vendor recourse and may increase financial exposure if we have repeated outages. Deal desk and ops recommend the exception given strategic value; Legal will add tight language.

Approval requested: Please reply with APPROVE or DENY and any amendment language by COB Monday. If approved, Marissa will prepare the amendment and route for signature (DocuSign link included).

Thanks —
David
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exec signoff request — Cobalt Tech service-credit cap (DEAL-8421)

Team —

APPROVE, with a minor modification: cap cumulative service credits to one invoice month in any 12-month period, and limit remedies strictly to service credits (no termination, no liquidated damages). Additionally require:

1) Root-cause analysis submitted within 7 business days for any SLO incident.
2) A remediation plan with milestone commitments for repeat incidents; if an account has 3 creditable incidents in a rolling 12-month window, the account will be reviewed by Execs for potential contract remediation (renewal negotiation, pricing change).
3) Legal to insert explicit language that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for SLO breaches in the amendment.

Marissa — proceed to prepare the amendment and send for signatures. Grace — please confirm operational readiness and the monitoring hooks.

Aditya Rao
CEO (interim) | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Signed_Amendment_DK-8421.pdf (application/pdf)
